items.title: Purchasing and Property Management

data.abstract: This proposed rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC) definition of "capital improvement" by removing the threshold amount of LSC funds that must be expended on an improvement to real estate for the expenditure to qualify as a capital improvement. The proposed amendment would distinguish the definition of a capital improvement from the monetary thresholds required for prior approval; promote consistent tracking and oversight of LSC funds used for capital improvements; and strengthen accountability for LSC funds invested in recipients' real property.

items.title: Cost Standards and Procedures; Purchasing and Property Management

data.abstract: This final rule revises the Legal Services Corporation's (LSC or Corporation) regulations governing cost allowability, prior approval requirements, and property and procurement standards applicable to LSC recipients. The final rule clarifies when recipients must obtain prior approval for expenditures of LSC funds; increases the monetary threshold for prior approval; clarifies the treatment of proceeds from fundraising activities supported with LSC funds; provides additional flexibility in LSC's review of prior approval requests; clarifies documentation requirements for prior approval requests; and revises the deadline and requirements for accounting for LSC funds invested in real estate. These amendments are intended to clarify existing requirements, reduce administrative burden, promote consistent oversight and enforcement, and strengthen accountability in the use of Federal funds.

items.title: Submission for OMB Review; Comment Request; Correction
Deepwater Port Application Processing and Licensing

data.abstract: This document proposes procedures for the processing of applications for the licensing of deepwater ports. The proposed rule reflects the transfer of deepwater port license application processing management under the Deepwater Port Act from the United States Coast Guard (USCG) to MARAD. Pursuant to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026 (2026 NDAA), MARAD is the Federal lead agency for purposes of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (NEPA) for all deepwater port license applications. USCG responsibility for authorities pertaining to design, construction, equipment, operation of deepwater ports, and navigational safety are not affected by the 2026 NDAA statutory changes, or this proposed rule and will continue to be administered by USCG.

Safety Zone; FRL Inaugural Invitational eFoil Exhibition Race, Miami Marine Stadium Basin, Miami, FL; Correction

data.abstract: The Coast Guard is correcting the comment submission deadline in its notice of proposed rulemaking published October 19, 2026, proposing to establish a temporary safety zone for the FRL Inaugural Invitational eFoil Exhibition Race in the Miami Marine Stadium Basin, Miami, Florida. This correction shortens the comment period so the Coast Guard may consider timely submitted comments before determining whether to issue a final rule in advance of the event.

items.title: Approval and Promulgation of State Plans for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Arizona; Control of Emissions From Existing Municipal Solid Waste Landfills

data.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a State plan submitted by the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD). This plan pertains to the regulation of landfill gas and its components from existing municipal solid waste (MSW) landfills. Maricopa's county plan was submitted in response to the EPA's promulgation of Emissions Guidelines and Compliance Times for MSW landfills. This action is being taken under the Clean Air Act (CAA).

items.title: Approval and Promulgation of Delegation of Authority for Designated Facilities and Pollutants; Allegheny County; Delegation of Authority of the Federal Plan for Existing Municipal Solid Waste Landfills

data.abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a request from the Allegheny County Health Department (ACHD) for delegation of authority to implement and enforce the Federal Plan requirements for existing Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) landfills within Allegheny County in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. On May 21, 2021, the EPA promulgated the Federal Plan for MSW landfills to fulfill the requirements of section 111(d) of the Clean Air Act (CAA). The Federal Plan addresses the implementation and enforcement of the emission guidelines applicable to existing MSW landfills located in areas not covered by an approved and currently effective State plan. The Federal Plan imposes emission limits and other control requirements for existing MSW landfills which will reduce designated pollutants.

tags: Civil Rights Cold Case Records Review Board

agencies: Civil Rights Cold Case Records Review Board
data.abstract: The Civil Rights Cold Case Records Review Board previously reviewed and made formal disclosure determinations on records related to civil rights cold case incident 2023-002-013 in which the Department of Justice (DOJ) proposed postponements. The DOJ later proposed one additional postponement. On October 27, 2026, the Review Board rejected this additional postponement. By issuing this notice, the Review Board complies with the Civil Rights Cold Case Records Collection Act of 2018 that requires the Review Board to publish in the Federal Register its determinations on the disclosure or postponement of records in the Collection no more than 14 days after the date of its decision.

Air Plan Revisions; Arizona; Maricopa County Air Quality Department; New Source Review; Emission Reduction Credits

data.abstract: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is taking final action to approve a revision to the Maricopa County Air Quality Department (MCAQD or "Department") portion of the Arizona State Implementation Plan (SIP). This revision establishes a federally enforceable program allowing for the generation of emission reduction credits (ERCs) by retrofitting or replacing existing on-road vehicles with lower emitting vehicles while meeting other Clean Air Act (CAA or "Act") requirements. These ERCs are intended to be used as offsets for major stationary sources under the Department's Nonattainment New Source Review (NNSR) program. The EPA is approving this SIP revision because we find that it meets the applicable CAA requirements.
